eligibility.quote: UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 15: invalid start byte

failed_conditions.quote: There is a heavy mismatch here between the message/C++ types and Python types. `string` is 8-bit data which does not have encoding, neither does `std::string`. Message strings *ought* to be UTF-8, but this is not enforced. But Python strings always enforce an encoding. So it is perfectly possible to publish data from C++, which gets mangled when received in Python.

notes: Eligibility agreed at step 6 (topic interface; the encoding of the string value crossing the boundary is a representation_convention — arbitrary bytes from C++ vs strict UTF-8 decode in the generated Python type support). Elements field:std_msgs/String.data and topic:/topic are right. Loudness disagreement: the spec records loud_documented with detection_stage 'connect' and an evidence text claiming 'the consumer logs an incompatibility error naming the element before any data is exchanged' — no such connect-time error exists in this source. What the issue shows is a Python traceback raised inside _take_subscription during rclpy.spin, i.e. the failure itself observed while processing data at run time; there is no compiler/import error, md5/type mismatch at connection, incompatible-QoS event, claim error, or launch error. Per the definitions that is silent_documented with detection_stage run. Resolution recommended agreed: the maintainer's working demonstration was on a rolling source build with his own publisher (a different peer and distro), and the reporter's foxy composition with the backport was never shown working.
